subject.title: fix(security): close active April 4 transport and auth gaps

question: Should this stale security-hardening branch be rebased/split into current owner paths, or should maintainers first change the Discord mention, proxy, and auth-rotation policies it assumes?
rationale: The branch changes SSRF, auth-session invalidation, and Discord mention-delivery boundaries, and current main has moved the owning code paths enough that automation should not choose the policy or rebase shape alone.

options.title: Rebase Or Split Into Current Paths
options.body: Refresh this work onto current main, remove the changelog edit, and repair the proxy, auth, and Discord policy coverage before merge consideration.

options.title: Approve A Broader Policy Shift
options.body: Maintainers can deliberately keep fail-closed proxy validation and blanket mention neutralization, but should state the upgrade and delivery impact and require matching poll coverage.

options.title: Close And Rebuild Later
options.body: If the branch remains tangled with later refactors, close this stale PR and open smaller current-main security PRs for the still-valid gaps.

recommendation.title: Rebase Or Split Into Current Paths
recommendation.body: Refresh this work onto current main, remove the changelog edit, and repair the proxy, auth, and Discord policy coverage before merge consideration.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the live PR and have recent merged history in the provider request and config-write paths involved in the rebase.
